newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends higher on arbitrage, Elf strike.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends higher on arbitrage, Elf strike.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended modestly higher on Wednesday, extending this week's gains after the strike at three French refineries entered its seventh day and the arbitrage to the U.S. stayed open.
"The market is very thin as far as barges are concerned. Consequently the market can move up or down based on a 1,000 tonne deal," said one trader.
"If you look at the difference between New York Harbor and European prices, you can see the arbitration is wide open and that might be pulling the barge market up," he said.
Eurograde barges rose $4 to $220/$222 fob ARA with Rotterdam refinery material trading at $222 and $222.50.
Regular unleaded barges rose a sharper $6 to $212/$216, narrowing the spread to premium unleaded slightly in what traders said was very thin interest.
Cargoes were notionally assessed at $228/$230 cif.
Traders shrugged off larger-than-expected increases in U.S. gasoline inventories as NYMEX gasoline continued to rally to its contract highs touched on Tuesday.
The trader said German gasoline demand was fully satisfied with refinery turnarounds nil and production cranked up to take advantage of rich margins.

But bullish traders cited the strike at the Elf refineries that has shut in 100,000 barrels per day of gasoline production and news on Wednesday that unions called for a 24-hour strike on Monday at Shell's 128,000 bpd Berre refinery in southern France.
